HAL raises his eyes to IRIS

questions.question: Viewer reads: he gives the key back to her - carried by: HAL
0-3s HOLD: does this happen on screen - HAL looks at the key on the table for a long moment, quite still?
3-4s ACTION: does this happen on screen - HAL raises his eyes to IRIS?
4-7s ACTION: does this happen on screen - HAL speaks to IRIS, gently?
7-8s HOLD: does this happen on screen - HAL's face softens?
Happens exactly once (not repeated or looped): HAL speaks to IRIS
HAL: does the face/body read as letting go, tender (restrained)? Must NOT read as: tears.
Line 43 is audible, spoken by the right character, lips match: HAL: Keep the key. The lock never changed.
HAL sounds like the voice bible: low gravelly male voice; no reference take yet (the first accepted speaking take becomes it)
Planned size CLOSE, EYE_LEVEL, STATIC: does the take match?

First frame matches state SC04_g1: Continues from the previous shot: IRIS standing across the table, frame-left; HAL seated at the table, frame-right; the key: flat on the table in front of the empty chair; the mugs: two white mugs on the table, the second one steaming beside the key; the empty chair: pulled out from the table on the left.

Last frame matches state SC04_g2: Continues from the previous shot: IRIS standing across the table, frame-left; HAL seated at the table, frame-right; the key: flat on the table in front of the empty chair; the mugs: two white mugs on the table, the second one steaming beside the key; the empty chair: pulled out from the table on the left.
Identity, wardrobe, set and light stable; no morphing, extra limbs, text artefacts or flicker.
Motion is physically plausible and smooth (full clip, not stills).
Line 43: does HAL clearly speak to IRIS (eyes and body toward them)?
Is the place where IRIS stands kept out of frame (never shown empty), and do HAL's eyes go just past the lens to frame-left?
Does HAL look at IRIS and never into the lens?

instructions: Fill checks[] (result, severity on FAIL, level, evidence, reviewer human:<id>), then `film.py review --film DIR --ingest FILE`. Leave a group UNASSESSED if you did not look.
